comparison.objective: Candidate attaches a rack rail to fixed posts; record refits a loaded drawer onto already installed roller slides and pull-tests it.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require bimanual leveling and engagement of a long sliding assembly. Candidate aligns spring prongs into rack holes, preserves front engagement while telescoping to the rear, and drives screws; record carries a loaded drawer above riding height so hidden hooks clear rollers, lowers it onto rails, closes, and reopens it.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate checks four post latches, spring extension, matched rack units, prescribed screws, and 3 s self-support; record checks drawer riding height/level/square pose, closure history, 30–80 mm pull-test opening, retained load, and 1 s release.
comparison.reason: Close at the generic slide-alignment level, but the interfaces and failure tests differ: rack-post latch installation versus hidden hook-over-roller engagement verified by drawer travel. Candidate needs explicit level, insertion, retention-load, and pull-test-like tolerances.
